item.title: Crestview to Host America 250 Grand Parade Saturday with Olympic Medalist as Grand Marshal
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Okaloosa County America 250 Commission is inviting the public to a historic parade celebration this Saturday, November 7, at 11 a.m. along Main Street in downtown Crestview. The event marks 250 years of American independence and is expected to draw one of the largest patriotic crowds in the county's history. The parade will feature vibrant…
item.content:encoded:
The Okaloosa County America 250 Commission is inviting the public to a historic parade celebration this Saturday, November 7, at 11 a.m. along Main Street in downtown Crestview. The event marks 250 years of American independence and is expected to draw one of the largest patriotic crowds in the county's history.

The parade will feature vibrant floats, marching bands, tributes to veterans, and participation from community organizations and cultural groups. Crestview native and Olympic speed skater Mia Manganello, who won a bronze medal for the United States at the February 2026 Winter Games in Milan, Italy, will serve as the parade's Grand Marshal. Organizers encourage attendees to wear red, white, and blue or period colonial attire.

The parade will be live-streamed on Facebook at facebook.com/okaloosacountyamerica250 and on YouTube at youtube.com/@EmeraldCoastTV for those unable to attend in person. If weather forces a cancellation, a makeup date has been scheduled for Sunday, November 8, at 2 p.m.

item.title: Surfin' Santa Parade Set for Dec. 6 on Pensacola Beach
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Pensacola Beach Chamber of Commerce is calling for parade entries ahead of this year's Surfin' Santa Beach Parade, a holiday tradition that draws thousands of families to the island. The parade is scheduled for Sunday, December 6, beginning at 2 p.m. from Avenida 10 and running down Via de Luna toward Casino Beach, ending at the Gulfside…
item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola Beach Chamber of Commerce is calling for parade entries ahead of this year's Surfin' Santa Beach Parade, a holiday tradition that draws thousands of families to the island.

The parade is scheduled for Sunday, December 6, beginning at 2 p.m. from Avenida 10 and running down Via de Luna toward Casino Beach, ending at the Gulfside Pavilion. Entry is open to local businesses, nonprofits, community organizations, and groups of friends. Registration fees are $50 for nonprofits and $100 for commercial businesses, with all fees nonrefundable.

Participants should check in and line up starting at 12:30 p.m. at the basketball courts (corner of Panferio Drive and Via de Luna Drive). Organizers will award prizes for the top three best-decorated floats.

Registration is now open through the Pensacola Beach Chamber of Commerce. More details are available on the chamber's website.

item.title: Pensacola Habitat for Humanity breaks ground on 9-home project at former Malcolm Yonge site
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Pensacola Habitat for Humanity will hold a groundbreaking ceremony Tuesday, November 10, at 10 a.m. for a nine-home affordable housing development on the former Malcolm Yonge Gymnasium property at 925 East Jackson Street. The project, developed in partnership with the City of Pensacola, aims to expand homeownership opportunities for residents who…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola Habitat for Humanity will hold a groundbreaking ceremony Tuesday, November 10, at 10 a.m. for a nine-home affordable housing development on the former Malcolm Yonge Gymnasium property at 925 East Jackson Street.

The project, developed in partnership with the City of Pensacola, aims to expand homeownership opportunities for residents who might otherwise struggle to afford a home in the area. The homes will be part of the Northwest Florida Community Land Trust, a structure designed to keep housing affordable for future generations of buyers.

Leaders from Pensacola Habitat for Humanity and city officials will speak at the ceremony about the vision for the neighborhood and provide additional details about the development. The organization is inviting the public and media to attend and help spread word about the opportunity to prospective homebuyers in the community.

item.title: Okaloosa County Sheriff warns of scam impersonating deputies
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Okaloosa County Sheriff's Office is alerting residents to a fraud scheme in which scammers are posing as law enforcement officials, including the chief deputy, to trick people out of money or information. While specific details about how the scam operates weren't immediately available, the sheriff's office is urging residents to be cautious…
item.content:encoded:
The Okaloosa County Sheriff's Office is alerting residents to a fraud scheme in which scammers are posing as law enforcement officials, including the chief deputy, to trick people out of money or information.

While specific details about how the scam operates weren't immediately available, the sheriff's office is urging residents to be cautious about unsolicited calls or contacts claiming to be from their agency. Officials remind the public that legitimate law enforcement will not solicit money over the phone or demand payment for fines or legal issues through unconventional means.

If you receive a suspicious call claiming to be from the Okaloosa County Sheriff's Office, hang up and contact the agency directly using a phone number you know to be legitimate. You can also report suspected scams to local law enforcement or the Florida Attorney General's office.

item.title: 111 Years Ago: Pensacola Bay Witnessed First Catapult Launch from Moving Ship
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: On this day in 1915, Pensacola Bay was the scene of a historic first in naval aviation. Lieutenant Commander Henry C. Mustin successfully launched an AB-2 seaplane from the armored cruiser USS North Carolina using a catapult while the ship was underway — a milestone that would shape the future of carrier-based aviation. The achievement marked a…
item.content:encoded:
On this day in 1915, Pensacola Bay was the scene of a historic first in naval aviation. Lieutenant Commander Henry C. Mustin successfully launched an AB-2 seaplane from the armored cruiser USS North Carolina using a catapult while the ship was underway — a milestone that would shape the future of carrier-based aviation.

The achievement marked a turning point in how the Navy could deploy aircraft at sea, moving beyond stationary launches from docked vessels. Mustin's flight from the USS North Carolina in Pensacola Bay demonstrated that aircraft could be rapidly launched during active operations, a capability that would become fundamental to modern naval warfare.

The feat reflects Pensacola's deep roots in naval aviation history. The area around NAS Pensacola has long been central to the development of carrier operations and aircraft launch systems that remain in use today.

item.content:encoded:
The Emerald Coast Utilities Authority will close its Customer Service Department on Wednesday, November 11, in observance of Veterans Day, the utility announced Thursday.

All other ECUA departments and offices will remain open during normal business hours. The closure will not affect residential or commercial sanitation collection schedules, which will continue on their regular routes.

Customers who need to reach ECUA during the closure can contact the utility on the following business day or through alternative service channels.

item.title: Escambia County's Peanut Butter Challenge Returns Through Nov. 20
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: UF/IFAS Escambia Extension is asking community members to donate unopened jars of peanut butter to support local food pantries through Friday, Nov. 20. The annual competition pits Florida counties against each other to collect donations, with Escambia County taking first place statewide last year by collecting 4,214 jars. Donations can be dropped…
item.content:encoded:
UF/IFAS Escambia Extension is asking community members to donate unopened jars of peanut butter to support local food pantries through Friday, Nov. 20. The annual competition pits Florida counties against each other to collect donations, with Escambia County taking first place statewide last year by collecting 4,214 jars.

Donations can be dropped off at 12 locations throughout Escambia County, including the county administration building, the Extension office on Stefani Road, Cordova Lanes, and several churches and libraries. Peanut butter was chosen as the donation item because of its nutritional value, long shelf life, and to highlight Florida's peanut production industry, which contributed over $168 million to the state's economy in 2025.

"Escambia County had incredible support from our community last year, and I hope to bring that same momentum to this year's challenge," said Nick Simmons, Escambia Extension Services Director. The Florida Peanut Producers Association and Florida Peanut Federation will also contribute to totals distributed to food pantries in their regions. For more information, contact Escambia Extension at 850-475-5230.

item.title: Historic SS United States scheduled to sink off Florida coast November 12
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The SS United States, a legendary ocean liner that once held the speed record for crossing the Atlantic, is set to be deliberately sunk off the Florida Gulf Coast on November 12 as an artificial reef. According to reporting from the Pensacola News Journal, the vessel—which served as a symbol of American maritime achievement during the Cold War…
item.content:encoded:
The SS United States, a legendary ocean liner that once held the speed record for crossing the Atlantic, is set to be deliberately sunk off the Florida Gulf Coast on November 12 as an artificial reef.

According to reporting from the Pensacola News Journal, the vessel—which served as a symbol of American maritime achievement during the Cold War era—will be scuttled in a controlled sinking operation. The ship has sat idle for years after being retired from service, and environmental and maritime officials have approved its use as a reef structure to support marine habitat.

The sinking represents an unconventional end for one of the most storied ships in U.S. maritime history. The SS United States earned fame in 1952 when it crossed the Atlantic in record time, a feat that stood for decades. The 990-foot vessel also served military and diplomatic purposes throughout its operational life before eventually being decommissioned.

item.title: City of Pensacola to close for Veterans Day, maintains sanitation schedule

All City administrative offices, City Hall, and community resource centers will be shuttered for the holiday. However, two facilities will remain open: Osceola Golf Course and…
item.content:encoded:
The City of Pensacola will close most municipal offices and facilities on Wednesday, November 11 in observance of Veterans Day, according to a city announcement Thursday.

All City administrative offices, City Hall, and community resource centers will be shuttered for the holiday. However, two facilities will remain open: Osceola Golf Course and Roger Scott Tennis Center will operate on their regular schedules.

Residents relying on sanitation services should note that collection schedules will continue unchanged during the week of November 9–15. The city urges anyone with questions to contact City Hall.

item.content:encoded:
Pensacola Fire Rescue responded to an animal rescue call Wednesday when a cat became trapped in a storm drain in the city. Firefighters were able to locate and safely remove the animal from the drain, adding another successful rescue to their growing list of calls that goes well beyond structure fires.

While much of the public sees firefighters primarily as responders to blazes, crews regularly handle a variety of emergency situations including animal rescues. The successful retrieval of the cat demonstrates the versatility and training of local fire rescue personnel.

No injuries were reported during the rescue operation.

item.title: Augusta Avenue Bridge Closes Nov. 10 for Rehabilitation Work
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County's Construction Management Division will shut down the Augusta Avenue Bridge to through traffic starting Tuesday, Nov. 10, for a comprehensive rehabilitation project on the bridge's existing structure. The closure is expected to last through December 2026, barring weather delays or other construction complications. Drivers will be…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County's Construction Management Division will shut down the Augusta Avenue Bridge to through traffic starting Tuesday, Nov. 10, for a comprehensive rehabilitation project on the bridge's existing structure. The closure is expected to last through December 2026, barring weather delays or other construction complications.

Drivers will be detoured to Atlanta Avenue and Selma Avenue during the work. The county urges motorists to exercise caution in the work zone and follow posted signs and road crew instructions. While the bridge itself will be closed to traffic, residents, pedestrians, local traffic, and emergency vehicles will retain access to properties within the work area, though some driveways and entrances may be temporarily blocked as crews move equipment and materials.

Construction schedules can shift due to weather or logistics, so the county advises drivers to check for updates before the closure takes effect.

item.title: Pensacola Woman Charged with Murder in Stabbing Initially Called Self-Inflicted
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A Pensacola woman was arrested Tuesday on a murder charge following a stabbing that authorities initially believed was self-inflicted, according to the Escambia County Sheriff's Office. Deputies arrested 29-year-old Kordaja Lakita Smith on November 4th and charged her with second-degree murder in connection with the fatal stabbing. The case…
item.content:encoded:
A Pensacola woman was arrested Tuesday on a murder charge following a stabbing that authorities initially believed was self-inflicted, according to the Escambia County Sheriff's Office.

Deputies arrested 29-year-old Kordaja Lakita Smith on November 4th and charged her with second-degree murder in connection with the fatal stabbing. The case represents a significant shift in the investigation after the incident was originally classified as self-inflicted.

The ECSO has not yet released additional details about the circumstances of the stabbing, the victim's identity, or what prompted investigators to reconsider their initial assessment. The arrest comes as detectives continue their investigation into the deadly incident.

item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County finished fiscal year 2025-2026 with more than $2 million in operational surplus, according to County Clerk and Comptroller Jason English.

The surplus represents unspent funds remaining after the county's operational budget cycle ended. County officials typically use such surpluses for contingencies, capital projects, or reserve accounts that help stabilize future budget planning.

English's report comes as local governments throughout Northwest Florida manage their finances heading into the new fiscal year.

item.content:encoded:
Several North Escambia and surrounding area high schools saw action this week, with dominant performances across the board.

On Wednesday night, Blountstown dominated Northview 34-6, while Marianna edged Jay 24-20 in a closer contest. Pace narrowly defeated Niceville 30-25 in another tight matchup.

Tuesday's slate featured some more lopsided scores. Tate overwhelmed Navarre 55-7, and Escambia shut out Gulf Breeze 30-0. Milton squeaked past Washington 14-12, while Pine Forest dominated Pensacola 40-0. South Walton also posted a shutout victory over West Florida, winning 28-0.

The postponement comes because youth football playoffs are taking over Anthony Pleasant Park this weekend, leaving no venue for the race. The event was originally planned for October 10 before…
item.content:encoded:
The Century Lions Club has rescheduled its Cross Country 5K Run/Walk for the second time, moving the event from this Saturday, November 7, to spring 2027.

The postponement comes because youth football playoffs are taking over Anthony Pleasant Park this weekend, leaving no venue for the race. The event was originally planned for October 10 before Hurricane Isaias forced an initial reschedule to November.

Century residents and participants should mark their calendars for a spring date to be announced by the Lions Club.
